claims.hypothesis: Do protostellar dust disk masses and radii decrease from Class 0 to Flat Spectrum?
claims.experiment: Gaussian fits to 0.87 mm continuum, mass and radius distributions via survival analysis
claims.result: Mean masses 25.9/14.9/11.6 Earth masses; mean radii 44.9/37.0/28.5 au
claims.finding: Masses decrease with evolution; radii decrease or stay constant, contrary to disk-growth predictions (dust radii only)

evidence.quote: The decrease in dust disk masses is expected from disk evolution and accretion, but the decrease in disk radii may point to the initial conditions of star formation

claims.hypothesis: Are protostellar disks more massive than Class II disks?
claims.experiment: Compare Orion mass distributions with Class II surveys
claims.finding: Solid growth toward planet cores may begin in protostellar phase

evidence.quote: The protostellar dust disk mass distributions are systematically larger than that of Class II disks by a factor of $>$4

claims.hypothesis: Do disk properties vary with region in Orion?
claims.experiment: Log-rank tests among northern ISF, L1641+southern ISF, Orion B

evidence.quote: These properties are not found to vary significantly between different regions within Orion.

claims.hypothesis: Are large (>50 au) protostellar disks common?
claims.experiment: Count disks with deconvolved 2σ radius >50 au

evidence.quote: At least 146 protostellar disks (35% out of 379 detected 0.87 mm continuum sources plus 42 non-detections) have disk radii greater than 50 au in our sample.

why_this_data.value: Orion provides a much larger protostar sample; VLA 9 mm probes optically thick inner disks

evidence.quote: even at submillimeter wavelengths the protostellar disks can be optically thick; therefore, VLA observations at 9 mm are crucial to examine the inner disks

why_this_method.value: Gaussian fitting is simple and fast for large samples; curve-of-growth and Nuker profiles less suited with envelopes

evidence.quote: While Gaussian fitting has limitations, its advantage lies in its simplicity and ability to rapidly fit a large number of sources.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Curve of growth and Nuker profile radius methods judged less suitable for protostellar disks

evidence.quote: These methods and assumptions are not always possible and/or reliable for protostellar disks, due in large part to the surrounding envelope.

limitations_admitted.value: Optically thick emission yields mass underestimates; envelope contamination possible; Gaussian radius biases

evidence.quote: If the dust emission is not optically thin, then the masses will be lower limits.

referee_caveats_inferred: Single-Gaussian radius definition not comparable with 90%-flux radii of other surveys
Mass depends on assumed opacity and L-scaled temperature; Perseus/Ophiuchus discrepancies unresolved
Distance from neural-net interpolation uncertain (flat 10 pc error)
Median/mean statistics mix multiples sharing one Lbol
